full.rationale: Rust payload rebaselined 2026-08-10 for 1.10.0: +449,536 bytes over the 1.8.4 reference, overrunning the 256 KiB allowance by 187,392 bytes. That number is not creep, it is ONE NEW TRACKED BINARY: st2k_dlghook.dll is 187,904 bytes, and this release is the first to count it, because it is the first release in which it exists. It is the Open/Save-dialog selection reader, a separate cdylib because it is loaded into other applications by a WH_CALLWNDPROC hook, and it was deliberately added to the counted set in check-release-size.ps1 and check-release-rust-payload.ps1 rather than left uncounted: an untracked shipped binary is how a payload budget quietly stops meaning anything. The remaining 261,632 bytes are 1.9.0 and 1.10.0 application growth measured against a 1.8.4 baseline, i.e. two releases, and they fit inside the allowance on their own. The INSTALLER budget is UNCHANGED and did NOT trip: 13,575,905 bytes against a 13,635,341 limit, 59,436 bytes of headroom, so its reference stays calibrated to the 1.8.4 artifact whose SHA-256 is recorded above (the reference must track a SHIPPED artifact, and Inno output is not byte-reproducible, so it is never set from a preparation build). Magick budget UNCHANGED and was not what tripped. The ARM64 entry below was rebaselined the same day from its own measured cross-build; see its rationale, and note its hook DLL is a different size because it is a real aarch64 binary. Previous rationale, still applicable to the pre-1.10.0 portion of this payload: Rust payload rebaselined 2026-08-08 for 1.8.4: +287,744 bytes over the 1.7.5 reference, which overran the previous 256 KiB allowance by 25,600 bytes. The growth is the 1.8.x work measured against a 1.7.5 baseline, not one release's worth: the QuickLook-parity preview batch and its transport strip, the SQLite database view, the portable registration path, and 1.8.4's own additions - the icon-style format badge (src/badge.rs: a seven-tint category palette and the dog-eared page silhouette), src/checkerpx.rs, src/typeoverlay.rs, and three new doctor checks including the shell round-trip that finally distinguishes 'our decoder works but Explorer drops it' (issue #16). The INSTALLER reference moved with it, to 1.8.4: the compressed setup grew 132,710 bytes over the 1.7.5 reference and overran the 128 KiB allowance by 1,638 bytes, which is the same Rust growth after compression and not a new payload. The magick budget is UNCHANGED and was not what tripped. The 1.7.5 rationale (the from-scratch JPEG 2000 reduced-resolution decoder in src/decode/jp2) still holds and is still in this payload. Keep later releases within 128 KiB compressed and 256 KiB for each raw payload unless an explicit reviewed policy change records why.

ARM64 Rust payload rebaselined 2026-08-10 for 1.10.0 from a MEASURED cross-build, not from the x64 number: +409,600 bytes over the 1.8.5 reference, overrunning the 256 KiB allowance by 147,456 bytes. Same one-new-binary cause as x64, and this is why it had to be measured rather than copied: st2k_dlghook.dll is 184,320 bytes here against 187,904 on x64, because it is a genuine aarch64 build rather than the x64 artifact travelling. The rest is 1.9.0 and 1.10.0 growth against a 1.8.5 baseline, two releases, which fits the allowance on its own. The INSTALLER budget is UNCHANGED and did NOT trip: 12,341,735 bytes against a 12,400,605 limit, 58,870 bytes of headroom, so its reference stays calibrated to the SHIPPED 1.8.5 artifact whose SHA-256 is recorded below (Inno output is not byte-reproducible, so an installer reference is never set from a preparation build). This ARM64 pass is also what caught the release pipeline never BUILDING the hook DLL: x64 had passed only because an earlier hand build had left one in the target directory, and ARM64, with no such leftover, failed at the staging copy. Magick budget UNCHANGED and was not what tripped. Previous rationale, still applicable to the pre-1.10.0 portion of this payload: ARM64 installer AND Rust payload rebaselined 2026-08-09 for 1.8.5. Same stale-reference shape as the 1.8.0 entry this replaces: the installer reference was still 12,146,914 bytes from 1.8.0-arm64-full-stubbed while x64 was rebaselined at 1.8.4, so the 137,412 bytes measured here are FIVE releases of accumulated, already-reviewed growth (1.8.1 through 1.8.5), not one release's worth. It overran the 128 KiB installer allowance by 6,340 bytes. Evidence that 1.8.5 itself is not the cause: x64, whose reference IS current (1.8.4), grew only 5,150 bytes of installer and 31,232 bytes of payload in this same release and passed with 125,922 bytes of headroom. The growth is the work x64 already absorbed at its 1.8.4 rebaseline - the icon-style format badge (src/badge.rs), src/checkerpx.rs, src/typeoverlay.rs and the doctor shell round-trip - plus 1.8.5's own src/vcodec.rs (video codec identification and the Media Foundation decoder probe). The Rust payload is rebaselined in the SAME edit rather than left alone: it PASSED, but with only 47,104 bytes of headroom (215,040 of its 256 KiB allowance already consumed against that same stale 1.8.0 reference), so leaving it would hand the next release a near-exhausted budget and a failure that has nothing to do with that release either. Magick budget UNCHANGED and was not what tripped. Installer 12269533 bytes, SHA-256 e7f3fc1974cae2f7d5f74a22e8a83d0b150bf52cef2363654edde111d26aa2a8 - the artifact PUBLISHED as v1.8.5. Note the installer is not byte-reproducible between builds (Inno Setup): the first 1.8.5 arm64 build measured 12,284,326 bytes / e187e5c2d61c..., and the release rebuild came out 14,793 bytes smaller. The reference always tracks the SHIPPED artifact, so a future comparison is against something a user can actually download and hash. Keep later releases within 128 KiB compressed and 256 KiB for each raw payload unless an explicit reviewed policy change records why. The stubs are built with the MSVC ARM64 toolchain (cl + link /DEF /IMPLIB) rather than MinGW, because MinGW emits x86_64 PEs regardless of target - the first ARM64 Full build silently replaced genuine ARM64 DLLs with x64 stubs, which an ARM64 loader refuses. gendef still extracts the exports for both architectures, since a PE export table is architecture-independent. link's /IMPLIB is load-bearing: without it the linker drops <name>.lib and <name>.exp beside /OUT, straight into the shipped bundle. harfbuzz and fribidi end up fully pruned once stubbing removes their importers, which is why the file count is 155. Every staged PE is asserted to be machine 0xAA64. NOTE: published 1.6.0 shipped the UNSTUBBED arm64 payload (13,589,408-byte installer); this reference applies from the next release.
